Apple today accused a new UK proposal targeting App Store fees as tantamount to price regulation, warning it could undermine innovation and investment. Details below.

Apple Defends App Store Regulation in UK

According to Reuters, Apple today filed a formal response to a consultation by the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), opposing a proposed rule that would allow app developers to link to alternative payment options.

The CMA designated both Apple and Google as having "strategic market status" in their respective mobile platform markets last year, after which it can impose relevant requirements. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, this designation enables the regulator to introduce company-specific rules to promote competition and give consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still charge commissions on transactions completed through alternative payment methods, but any associated fees must be deemed "fair and reasonable."

Reuters noted that the CMA "expects onboarding fees to be lower than current App Store charges, with savings passed on to UK consumers or reinvested in developer businesses to support innovation."

However, Apple disagrees and opposes the proposal. Reuters reports as follows:

and

The CMA rejected Apple's characterization of the proposal as price regulation, stating it aims to set principles for determining whether onboarding fees are fair and reasonable, rather than directly setting fee levels.
